map.以「乾为天」为例读取卦象: Reading a hexagram using "Qian (The Creative / Heaven)" as an example
map.乾卦为六十四卦第 1 卦（卦序 1），上下皆乾（☰），六爻皆阳，卦辞“元亨利贞”: Qian is the 1st of the 64 hexagrams (sequence 1); both upper and lower trigrams are Qian (☰), all six lines are yang, its judgment is 'Yuan Heng Li Zhen' (primordial, flourishing, beneficial, correct), symbolizing strength and vigor. Its inverse is Kun (☷, all yin); its complementary is also Qian (self-symmetric). The changed hexagram, when the initial yang line changes, becomes Tian Feng Gou (䷫, Heaven and Wind, Coming to Meet). The table lets you quickly locate the name, sequence, upper/lower trigrams, and basic pronouncements.
map.六十四卦是怎么由八卦组合出来的？: How are the 64 hexagrams formed from the 8 trigrams?
map.以三爻经卦两两相重（下卦×上卦）得六爻别卦，共 8×8=64 种。每卦有固定卦序: The 64 hexagrams come from combining the 8 three-line trigrams in pairs (lower trigram x upper trigram), giving 8 x 8 = 64 six-line hexagrams. Each has a fixed sequence (the standard Zhouyi order or the Jing Fang Eight Palaces order) and is paired with a name and judgment; they are the core of I Ching divination and philosophical study.
map.卦序和卦名有什么用？: What are the sequence number and name for?
map.卦序便于检索与记忆（如乾 1、坤 2、屯 3、蒙 4…），卦名概括一卦主旨（如“: The sequence aids lookup and memory (e.g., Qian 1, Kun 2, Zhun 3, Meng 4 …), and the name summarizes a hexagram's theme (e.g., 'Tai' denotes heaven and earth communicating, 'Pi' denotes heaven and earth not communicating). After casting, you can look up by sequence or by upper/lower trigram to locate the primary and changed hexagrams.
